key_insight: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks exploit neural-network hierarchy to process weight-space graphs more efficiently than flat graph metanetworks while preserving permutation symmetries.
engineering_relevance: H-GMNs enable deeper metanetworks for evaluating, testing and editing large neural networks without the memory growth of flat graph processing.
method: Represent neural networks as graphs organised into neuron, layer and block levels.
Coarsen and refine graphs using permutation-symmetry-preserving pooling and unpooling.
Extend hierarchical processing to Transformers with a symmetry-preserving graph construction.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on ResNet-18 and ViT model zoos with models up to 86M parameters cover Lipschitz-bound proxy, generalisation and robustness prediction, backdoor detection and pruning, reporting improved sample efficiency and nearly constant cost as metanetwork depth grows.
watch_item: Nearly constant cost is reported with increasing metanetwork depth, not increasing input-model size; architecture-specific graph construction remains an implementation consideration.
